subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjectFacilities
subsystem.responsibility: Heterogeneous set of generic runtime object facilities evidenced in isolation: cleanup/destructor patterns for pointer containers and linked lists, bounds-checked list-entry string accessors, string formatting and unit conversion helpers, physics coefficient and quadratic evaluation objects, a scene-node transform decoder, vehicle object construction and physics-state fields, and session-lifecycle post-processing handlers. Grouping is structural (shared this-field offsets and shared callers), not evidence of original source organization.

summary: Conservative architecture for 27 validated runtime-object functions. Dominant patterns: (1) teardown routines gated on a this+0x8 enable byte that free a data block and optionally the container (TextDisplayStructure, LinkedListContainer, DestructorWithDoubleFreePattern); (2) bounds-checked indexed accessors returning the first char* of a linked-list entry with a global fallback (StringListContainerA/B, SubObjectPropertyWrapper, DirectoryListSorter); (3) display formatters sharing a this+0x4 unit/selection flag, the byte_5C3734/byte_5C3738 unit strings and StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck (MenuDisplayFormatter); (4) small double-coefficient physics objects evaluated on the per-frame path (QuadraticSpringModel, QuadraticFormMatrix); (5) a large vehicle/physics state object whose fields span this+0x0..this+0x453C (VehicleObject) including construction-time reference stores, lateral torque output, wheel target setter and the AI target-vehicle pointer; (6) session-lifecycle global-driven handlers (DynManPostProcessor, SessionTypeHandler). Most owners are UNKNOWN in the packet; class boundaries and field names are DERIVED/GUESS proposals only.

function_roles.role: Scene-node transform decoder: decodes a 6-bit node-group type and 16-bit node index from the packed node header, dispatches via jump table 0x00411100 into six node groups, bounds-checks the index against the group count, resolves a target pointer as base + stride*idx + 208, and forwards a decoded 24-byte transform (six floats) to the transform consumer at 0x0054B4D0.

Two-phase initializer for a 537-entry table of (range, random-offset) 16-bit pairs behind this: defaults every pair to (1, 0), then for index bands 1..290 (word_5BEBB0) and 293..535 (word_5BF2F8) derives a range from the boundary tables via TableLookupByIndex and draws a random offset via RandLCGRandomNumberGenerator; indices {0, 291, 292, 536} keep the default.

Deep cleanup of a text display structure: when this+0x8 is set and the data block at this+0x0 is non-null, reinitializes the block via TextFormatStructInitializer, frees nine internal pointers (eight at 5-dword stride plus the first) and the block via FreeWrapper_7bcf, then optionally frees the container when a2 bit 0 is set; returns this.

Destructor-like cleanup for a pointer container: if this+0x8 is non-zero and the data block *this is non-null, frees the first internal pointer and the block via FreeWrapper_7bcf; optionally frees the container when a2 bit 0 is set; returns this.
Unconditional global state reset: writes 0 into the four consecutive dwords dword_5EBB18..dword_5EBB24 and returns 0.

Linked-list teardown: walks the list whose head is at this+0x1A0, frees each node's data pointer when the node+8 byte flag is zero and frees every node via FreeWrapper_7bcf, then zeroes the four list-management fields this+0x1A0..0x1AC; returns the last FreeWrapper result.
Vehicle construction-time setter: stores the input at this[0] and again at this[0x4034], invoking F_4FieldPropagation on the input in between, and returns that call's result.

AI speed-delta helper: returns the difference of the float at +76 between a caller-supplied vehicle and the target vehicle pointer at this+0x4354; returns 0.0 for a null input and -1.0 when no target vehicle is set.

Lateral torque helper on the per-frame physics tick: multiplies the input force by the coefficient at this+0x44F4 and the fixed scaling constant 0.0099999998, storing the product into this+0x453C (a recalculated field).
Bulk construction loop: calls VehicleObjectConstructor on 104 slots starting at 0x005EC6D8 with stride 0x48C0 and returns the last constructor result.

DynMan post-processing handler: optionally logs a debug entry gated on StringSplitLoop, resets every vehicle in the array at 0x7C54F0 (count at 0x5C329C) via per-vehicle reset 0x004C6E80, initializes wheel dynamics from race-elapsed-time at 0x7C7428, resets season scoring, and destroys graphics resources through the global instance at 0x5EA560.
Single-purpose no-op passthrough: invokes an unresolved stub with the address of global dword_7C569C and returns the stub's result unchanged.

Weighted-ratio lookup over a 1D 8-byte-entry table: rejects negative / out-of-range indexes (count at this+0x8), non-positive base entries (this+0xC) and non-positive divisors (this+0x10); otherwise returns (scale*weight)/(base*divisor) using scale at this+0x14.

State-change event trigger: when the entity IDs at a2+16 and a3+16 match and the state at a3+20 differs from a2+20, copies the reference state into a3+20 and raises the flags at this+0x0 and this+0x19A4 to 1; returns the matched state.

Weighted-sum balancer: while a2's weighted sum (base + index*coefficient) exceeds a1's beyond a tolerance multiplier, decrements a2's index (when flag and index > 0) or increments a1's index (below maxIndex - 1), re-checking after each step.

UI message formatter: selects a format template by the this+0x4 flag (byte_5C3738 vs byte_5C3734), resolves it through BinarySearchInStringTable into byte_5EC4CC, then formats with the argument table off_5C3730 via StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck.

Physics-state pressure/force field mapping: builds blend factors from tire surface-contact floats (this+0x1CA8/0x1CAC/0x1CB0/0x1CB4), clamps grid-index fields via PositionIndexClamp, fills a local table via SessionStateIndexedLookup, runs a minimum-deviation index search over this+0x1640/0x1644 entries and a nearest-index loop over this+0x16C0/0x16C4 elements (stride 0x40).

Temperature formatter: converts Kelvin to Celsius (a2 - 273.16), optionally to Fahrenheit when this+0x4 == 1, selects the unit string (byte_5C3738 Fahrenheit / byte_5C3734 Celsius) and formats the integer plus unit via the "%d %s" template with StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck.
Unconditional flagged setter on the wheel-dynamics path: stores the input as a dword at this+0x1CBC and raises the byte flag at this+0x1CB8 to 1; returns the input.

Telemetry triplet formatter: reads three consecutive Kelvin floats from the index-derived temperature array, converts to Celsius, optionally to Fahrenheit by the this+0x4 flag, formats either the full triplet ("%3d/%3d/%3d %s") or a single value, clears a per-index flag byte, and returns the format result.

Bounds-checked indexed list-entry accessor (container layout A): rejects out-of-range indexes against the count at *(this)+0x2C, walks the list from the head at *(this)+0x20 via next pointers at node+4, and returns the first char* at entry-data+0, falling back to byte_5EA438 for a null string.
Wrapper accessor: dereferences this[0] to a sub-object and returns the DWORD at sub-object offset 0x3C.

Bounds-checked indexed list-entry accessor (container layout B, offsets +0x30/+0x3C instead of +0x20/+0x2C): structurally identical to 0x00432820, walking next pointers at node+4 and returning the first char* at entry-data+0 with the byte_5EA438 fallback.

Cleanup wrapper: resets the shared AI state buffer at byte_7C56C0 via AIStateBufferInitialize and copies the default application-directory path byte_5EA438 into the object's path buffer via StringCopyWithBufferRealloc, returning the copy result.

Merge sort over a singly linked list of string entries with the result head/tail stored into this[0]/this[4]/this[8]: splits at the midpoint, recursively sorts both halves, merges in ascending order with a 2-byte-stride lexicographic comparison (null strings fall back to byte_5EA438) and reconnects head and tail.

3-axis quadratic form evaluator: per axis selects one of two 3-element coefficient rows of `this` by the sign of a2[i], accumulates row * a2[i]^2 into a 3-double output copied to a4, and builds an anti-symmetric 3-element output a5 from this+0x90/0x98/0xA0 scaled by a3[i]^2, negated when a3[i] is positive.
Quadratic spring evaluation: evaluates two quadratics at a2 (force set from +0x4/+0xC/+0x14 into +0x34; derivative set from +0x1C/+0x24/+0x2C into +0x3C) on the per-frame suspension solver path.

classes.name: SceneNodeDecoder
classes.responsibility: Decodes packed scene-node transforms by dispatching a 6-bit node-group type to one of six node groups, each holding a count and a base pointer; resolves base + stride*idx + 208 and forwards six decoded floats (rotations and packed position) to a transform consumer.

classes.name: RandomRangeTable
classes.responsibility: Owns a 537-entry table of (range, random-offset) 16-bit pairs populated at startup from two index-banded boundary tables and an LCG; most indices get randomized ranges, edge indices keep a (1, 0) default.

classes.name: TextDisplayStructure
classes.responsibility: Text-display container whose cleanup (and optionally container deletion) is gated on a this+0x8 enable byte; deep cleanup frees a set of internal pointers plus the data block, a shallow variant frees the first pointer only.

classes.name: GlobalStateReset
classes.responsibility: Resets four consecutive global dwords (dword_5EBB18..dword_5EBB24) to zero; purpose of the globals is unknown.

classes.name: LinkedListContainer
classes.responsibility: Holds a singly linked list (head at this+0x1A0) of nodes with +0 data, +4 next, +8 flag; teardown frees node data conditionally and every node, then zeroes the four list-management fields.

classes.name: VehicleObject
classes.responsibility: Large per-vehicle state object (offsets span this+0x0..this+0x453C within a 0x48C0-stride slot): construction-time reference store, AI target-vehicle pointer, lateral-torque coefficient and output, tire surface-contact floats and pressure/force-field index tables, and a flagged wheel target value setter. Field ownership is inferred from offset range and physics/AI context, not proven by the packet.

classes.name: VehicleArrayConstructor
classes.responsibility: Constructs the fixed 104-slot vehicle array at 0x005EC6D8 (stride 0x48C0) by calling VehicleObjectConstructor on each slot.

classes.name: DynManPostProcessor
classes.responsibility: Post-race (DynMan_Post) handler driven entirely by globals: optionally logs a debug entry, resets all live vehicles, initializes wheel dynamics from race elapsed time, resets season scoring, and destroys graphics resources.

classes.name: SessionTypeHandler
classes.responsibility: Per-session-type placeholder handler that passes the address of global dword_7C569C to an unresolved stub and returns its result.

classes.name: WeightedLookupTable
classes.responsibility: Reads a weighted ratio from a 1D 8-byte-entry table guarded by count, entry base and divisor; returns a scaled ratio or a 0.0 sentinel.

classes.name: StateChangeTrigger
classes.responsibility: Detects a state change on a tracked entity (entity ID at +16, state at +20) and raises two trigger flags on itself when the reference state differs.

classes.name: WeightedBalanceStruct
classes.responsibility: A weighted-sum struct (base at +0, coefficient at +8, maxIndex at +0x10, currentIndex at +0x14) whose current index is adjusted to balance two such structs within a tolerance.

classes.name: MenuDisplayFormatter
classes.responsibility: Menu/telemetry display formatting object sharing a this+0x4 selection/unit flag (1 selects the primary format buffer / Fahrenheit), the byte_5C3738 and byte_5C3734 unit/format strings, and safe string formatting via StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck; all three methods are called by MenuCommandDispatcher.

classes.name: StringListContainerA
classes.responsibility: Container (via a this[0] pointer) holding a linked list head at +0x20 and an entry count at +0x2C; provides bounds-checked indexed access to the first char* of each entry with a global fallback string.

classes.name: SubObjectPropertyWrapper
classes.responsibility: Thin wrapper over a sub-object reached through this[0]; reads a DWORD property at sub-object offset 0x3C.

classes.name: StringListContainerB
classes.responsibility: Container (via a this[0] pointer) holding a linked list head at +0x30 and an entry count at +0x3C; structurally identical accessor to StringListContainerA but with a different field group. Whether this is a second field group of the same class or a distinct class is unresolved.

classes.name: PathStateCleanup
classes.responsibility: Resets the shared AI state buffer and copies the default application-directory path into an object path field during cleanup.

classes.name: DirectoryListSorter
classes.responsibility: Merge sorts a singly linked list of string entries, storing the sorted head/tail (and a duplicate head) into this[0]/this[4]/this[8]; used during directory entry enumeration.

classes.name: QuadraticFormMatrix
classes.responsibility: 3-axis quadratic-form coefficient matrix with per-axis row selection by input sign and an anti-symmetric output built from this+0x90/0x98/0xA0; used on the suspension-force path.

classes.name: QuadraticSpringModel
classes.responsibility: Double-coefficient suspension spring model: evaluates force and derivative quadratics at a travel input and stores both results into the coefficient object.

interfaces.name: IStringListEntryAccessor
interfaces.purpose: Bounds-checked indexed retrieval of the first char* stored in a linked-list entry. Implementations reject out-of-range indexes with 0, walk the list via node+4 next pointers, read the entry data at node+0, and return the first string at data+0; a null string falls back to the global byte_5EA438. The two implementations use different container field groups (+0x20/+0x2C vs +0x30/+0x3C), so they are modeled as distinct classes behind a common behavioral interface.

compatibility_contracts.name: VehicleSlotArrayLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The game constructs 104 vehicle slots starting at 0x005EC6D8 with a stride of 0x48C0, each slot constructed by the vehicle constructor at 0x004C6920. A replacement must preserve this base/stride/count and the per-slot construction entry point.

compatibility_contracts.name: SceneNodeTransformDecode
compatibility_contracts.description: Packed scene-node headers encode a 6-bit node-group type and a 16-bit node index; the decoder dispatches into six node groups (stride 792, group D stride 808), resolves a target at base + stride*idx + 208, and converts the packed 24-byte transform into six floats using scale constants 0.00048828125 (rotation int16s at node+19/21/23) and 0.000030517578 (packed position across node+10..18), forwarding them to the transform consumer at 0x0054B4D0.

compatibility_contracts.name: RandomRangeTableInit
compatibility_contracts.description: A 537-entry table of (range, random-offset) 16-bit pairs is initialized to (1, 0) everywhere, then indices 1..290 and 293..535 are randomized from boundary tables word_5BEBB0 / word_5BF2F8 with the LCG at 0x005884ED; indices {0, 291, 292, 536} must keep the default.

compatibility_contracts.name: TextDisplayCleanupPattern
compatibility_contracts.description: Text-display containers gate cleanup on the byte flag at +0x8 and a non-null data block at +0x0. Deep cleanup frees nine internal pointers plus the block; a shallow variant frees the first pointer plus the block. When the caller's a2 bit 0 is set the container itself is freed as well. All frees go through FreeWrapper_7bcf.

compatibility_contracts.name: StringListEntryAccessorContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Indexed accessors over linked-list containers return 0 for out-of-range indexes, null nodes and null entry data, and return the first char* of the Nth entry (entry data at node+0, first string at data+0); a null string falls back to the global byte_5EA438. Both layout variants (+0x20/+0x2C and +0x30/+0x3C) must preserve this behavior.

compatibility_contracts.name: TemperatureDisplayUnits
compatibility_contracts.description: Display formatters convert Kelvin to Celsius by subtracting 273.16 and, when the unit flag at +0x4 equals 1, convert Celsius to Fahrenheit via (C + 40.0) * 1.8 - 40.0, selecting the byte_5C3738 (Fahrenheit) or byte_5C3734 (Celsius) unit string; formatting goes through StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck.

unresolved: Most function owners are UNKNOWN in the packet; the class boundaries proposed here (especially the broad VehicleObject grouping) are inferred from this-field offset ranges and shared callers, not proven. Per rule 8, equal offsets on different bases (e.g. obj:0x3C in both SubObjectPropertyWrapper and StringListContainerB) were not merged.
Behavior of the transform consumer 0x0054B4D0 on the six decoded floats is unknown; the meaning of the value returned to the caller LinkedListIteratorWithStateUpdate (0x004B5760) is not established.
The semantic mapping of the six node-group types and the reason for the stride difference (792 vs 808) in group D are not established.
The purpose and consumer of the 537-entry (range, random-offset) table, and the meaning of boundary indices {291, 292} and the two index bands, are unknown.
Whether the DestructorWithDoubleFreePattern (0x00418D60) double-free is intended depends on the caller contract; the element type behind *v3 is unknown.
Purpose of the four consecutive globals dword_5EBB18..dword_5EBB24 is unknown.
The node struct layout (+0 data, +4 next, +8 flag) in LinkedListContainer and the meaning of the node+8 flag are inferred from dereferences, not named by the packet.
The purpose of storing the input at both this[0] and this[0x4034] in 0x00424040 and what F_4FieldPropagation propagates into are unknown.

Read-only globals dbl_59E420, dbl_59E880 (0x004313C0), dbl_59E444 (0x0042AD00), dbl_59EAB0/59EAB8/59EAC0/59EAC8 and aDS 0x5C3778 (0x00431950/0x00431AA0) are flagged by packet facts but absent from the raw decompiled source; their roles (coefficient storage, temperature transform constants) are not deterministically tied.
The float at +76 in each vehicle in 0x00426CC0 is not proven to be the same quantity; field this+0x43A0 is accessed in the IDB but absent from the decompiled body.

The coefficient rows this[0..17] of QuadraticFormMatrix are read by the raw source but have no packet field entries; the fill's 'compression stiffness' label for 0x90/0x98/0xA0 conflicts with their use as anti-symmetric a5 coefficients.
The meaning of the second quadratic set in 0x00436470 as a 'derivative' comes from prior fill prose, not from this function alone.

The base/weight/divisor/scale roles in WeightedLookupTable and the weighted-sum field roles in 0x0042E4A0 are derived from arithmetic shape, not named by the packet; dbl_59E9F0 as tolerance is inferred.

The a2 argument of LinkedListMergeSort (0x00434090) is never referenced in the visible decompilation; the sort-result class and the wide-character (2-byte stride) comparison interpretation are DERIVED.

The unresolved stub callee of SessionTypeHandler (0x0042CE20) and the final graphics-resource destructor of DynManPostProcessor (0x0042C9F0) are absent from the packet callee table; their call targets are unknown.

Whether StringListContainerA (+0x20/+0x2C) and StringListContainerB (+0x30/+0x3C) are two field groups of one class or two classes is unresolved; they are modeled as distinct classes behind the shared IStringListEntryAccessor interface.

The unit/selection flag at this+0x4 is only observed as binary (1 vs else); the full set of meaningful values is not evident. The MenuDisplayFormatter grouping (three methods sharing this+0x4, the unit strings and caller 0x004674E0) is a DERIVED proposal, not proven common ownership.
Semantics of the index-derived temperature array base this + (3*a2 + 1851)*4 and the reset byte this + a2 + 7400 in 0x00431AA0, and of the a4 selector values other than 3, are not documented.
The returned char* of the two list accessors (a directory/file path per existing analysis) and the content of the default string byte_5EA438 are inferred, not established.
The role of the returned values in 0x004190C0 (last FreeWrapper result), 0x00431AA0 (format result) and 0x00434090 (trailing merge value) have no meaningful semantic contract.
